claim: OWASP explicitly forbids storing session identifiers or sensitive auth data in local storage because JavaScript can always read it.
quote: Do not store session identifiers in local storage as the data is always accessible by JavaScript. A single Cross Site Scripting can be used to steal all the data in these objects.

claim: The OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Apps BCP ranks BFF > token-mediating backend > browser-based public client, mandates refresh-token rotation or sender-constraining for browser clients, and warns malicious JS can run a hidden-iframe silent auth code flow regardless of storage.
quote: Authorization servers MUST either rotate refresh tokens on each use OR use sender-constrained refresh tokens; ... the attacker can inject a hidden iframe and launch a silent Authorization Code flow.

claim: In the BFF pattern the SPA holds only an httpOnly SameSite session cookie plus a CSRF header; tokens never reach the browser.
quote: The browser only ever holds a session cookie - it never sees tokens. Access and refresh tokens stay on the server.

claim: Third-party-cookie blocking (Safari ITP, Chrome) breaks iframe prompt=none silent renewal as a general mechanism.
quote: Because prompt=none in an iframe is no longer an option when third-party cookies are blocked, applications must adjust their sign-in patterns to have an authorization code issued.

claim: Rotating refresh tokens are the sanctioned replacement for iframe-based silent renew in SPAs affected by browser privacy controls.
quote: Refresh Token Rotation ... provides a secure method for using refresh tokens in SPAs while providing end-users with seamless access to resources without the disruption in UX caused by browser privacy technology like ITP.

claim: react-oidc-context is a lightweight React auth context provider built on oidc-client-ts, protocol-generic rather than IdP-specific.
quote: Lightweight auth library using the oidc-client-ts library for React single page applications (SPA). Support for hooks and higher-order components (HOC).

claim: oidc-client-ts is the underlying OIDC/OAuth2 protocol library implementing Authorization Code + PKCE and automatic silent renew for browser apps.
quote: Library to provide OpenID Connect (OIDC) and OAuth2 protocol support for client-side, browser-based JavaScript client applications.

claim: @axa-fr/react-oidc isolates tokens in a service worker so page JavaScript cannot read them - the strongest pure-SPA hardening short of a BFF.
quote: The service worker keeps tokens away from the JavaScript context.

claim: Keycloak deprecated its own adapters and directs users to standard OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect libraries.
quote: With the wide-spread availability of OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect libraries ... Keycloak is deprecating the adapters and focusing more on the Keycloak server, ... advocating better alternative options to Keycloak adapters.

claim: Context is for stable values; a client store like Zustand is only warranted for frequently-changing client-owned state - auth identity read from a provider does not need one.
quote: Use Context for genuinely static configuration values ... and a store for dynamic application state.

claim: Combining an HTTP-client 401-retry interceptor with TanStack Query's own retry logic causes duplicate refresh attempts; auth failures should be excluded from query retries and handled once centrally.
quote: What's the correct approach to use axios response interceptors with react-query having retries enabled
